channel.title: EU & Swiss News Feed
channel.description: Latest news from Europe covering politics, economy, and security

item.title: [EU Observer] After the poison of Saxony-Anhalt, Berlin election could be the antidote
item.description: We hear a lot about extremism in Germany, after the breakthrough of the AfD earlier this month. Yet a far-left government may be about to take power in Berlin on Sunday, and is attracting almost no attention. Why is that?

item.title: [DW] UK: Village votes to 'secede' in asylum center plan protest
item.description: Residents of Piddington, a tiny, remote village in Oxfordshire in England, have staged a "referendum" on leaving the UK. They are objecting to plans to open an asylum reception center at a disused military base nearby.

item.title: [DW] Can Canada and the EU deepen ties to counter Trump?
item.description: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney is known for standing up to US President Donald Trump. Now he wants to forge a "unique alliance" with Europe. But what could such a partnership look like?

item.title: [EU Observer] Von der Leyen’s ‘European values,’ paid for by private equity, powered by Claude
item.description: Ursula von der Leyen talks about European sovereignty and keeping Europe’s fate in European hands, but the model she presented for achieving that sovereignty relies heavily on non-European technology and global capital.

item.title: [DW] Shock in Kosovo as Hague convicts former President Thaci
item.description: The conviction in The Hague of former President Hashim Thaci and three former Kosovo Liberation Army leaders has caused consternation in Kosovo — both among political leaders and on the streets. DW reports from Pristina.

item.title: [EU Observer] Belgian minister under fire for denying evacuation to 13 Gazan scholarship students
item.description: Belgium's minister for migration was accused of being "the shame of this government" during a heated debate on Wednesday on the fate of 13 Gazans who won scholarships to Belgian universities but have been denied transport so that they can take up their places.

item.title: [DW] British-American writer Bonnie Greer dies aged 77
item.description: Chicago-born playwright Bonnie Greer, who became a familiar face in British political discourse later in life, has died. Her husband David Hutchins announced news of Greer's death.

item.title: [DW] Poland reaffirms support for Ukraine after drone strikes
item.description: After Russia's recent drone attacks on targets close to the Ukraine-Poland border, Warsaw has doubled down on its support for Kyiv and pledged a "nonprovocative but serious response" to Moscow.

item.title: [DW] Kosovo ex-president Thaci sentenced to 25 years for war crimes
item.description: A Hague tribunal ruled that Hashim Thaci, a former leader of the Kosovo Liberation Army (KLA), is responsible for war crimes carried out during the war of independence with Serbia.

item.title: [ECFR] An outsider within: The paradox of the Europe-Turkey relationship
item.description: Turkey is neither drifting away from the West nor is it coming home. It has become an embedded outsider: a middle power that has learned to build strategic autonomy from inside the Western system rather than by leaving it.

item.title: [ECFR] A future with Chinese characteristics
item.description: The world is undergoing a historical and cultural rupture. Just as Hollywood and other American exports once gave the rest of the world a glimpse of modern life and the future that awaited them, China is now doing the same for African, Latin American and even American young people

item.title: [ECFR] Friends without benefits: Why the EU should offer Canada more than casual defence ties
item.description: Trump is pushing Canada—a quiet military powerhouse—away from America. The EU should seize the chance and fold it into its own defence

item.title: [DW] Turkey's rights groups, EU call out LGBTQ+ crackdown
item.description: Several raids and arrests of LGBTQ+ persons in Turkey have triggered sharp criticism from numerous Turkish organizations — and also from Brussels.

item.title: [DW] Why do authoritarian regimes target the LGBTQ+ community?
item.description: A recent crackdown on the LGBTQ+ community in Turkey is symptomatic of a wider rights regression, according to experts. It's worse under authoritarian regimes, but why is it such a popular policy for these states?

item.title: [ECFR] Indian summer: The BRICS summit and warming New Delhi-Beijing relations
item.description: Xi Jinping’s attendance at the BRICS summit in New Delhi underlines the recent normalisation in Sino-Indian relations. This should encourage the EU to speed up its efforts to deepen ties with India

item.title: [ECFR] Life of the party: Democrats and the search for a post-Trump future
item.description: The race for US midterms reveals a rapidly changing Democratic party. Europeans must understand and engage its three camps well before the party could take power

item.title: [DW] Netherlands: Suspected sabotage disrupts train services
item.description: A major outage has hit parts of the Dutch railway system after objects were found placed across lines, authorities say. The company responsible for rail infrastructure says it suspects deliberate wrongdoing.

item.title: [DW] Europe launches two climate observation satellites
item.description: The European Space Agency has put two satellites into orbit to take a closer look at the impact of climate change. One of them will focus particularly on plant life.

item.title: [ECFR] Future nostalgia: Europe’s unfinished song
item.description: ECFR’s new research reveals Europeans are suffering from an imagination gap. Many people want to see Europe strong and flourishing—but fewer can picture a credible route from today’s disruptions to that destination

item.title: [ECFR] Beyond Saxony-Anhalt: What Merz’s crisis means for Europe
item.description: The far-right AfD’s win in a small German state calls for dynamism in Berlin and hedging in Brussels

item.title: [ECFR] Emergency Room: The AfD’s victory in Saxony-Anhalt
item.description: Mark Leonard welcomes Jana Puglierin, senior policy fellow and head of ECFR’s Berlin office, to discuss the Alternative for Germany (AfD)’s election win in Saxony-Anhalt—and what it means for Germany and Europe

item.title: [ECFR] Britons back ban on trade with Israeli settlements by more than two to one
item.description: New polling published by ECFR shows that Britons across the political divide favour banning trade with illegal Israeli settlements

item.title: [Financial Times] Trump administration approves $24bn sale of F-35 jets to Saudi Arabia
item.description: Deal comes amid escalation in Middle East conflict — but transfer likely to face opposition in US Congress

item.title: [Politico Europe] Who needs Parliament?
item.description: If you’ve been forwarded this newsletter, you can sign up free here. ESSENTIALS — Tony Burke’s migration reveal — Labor’s ‘Anyone but Shoebridge’ ultimatum to Greens — The inevitable veterans’ health cap backflip DRIVING THE DAY MIGRATION VIBE CHECK Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke treated his National Press Club audience like adults. And we all […]

item.title: [DW] Russian birth tourism to Brazil increases
item.description: Since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine and stricter regulations in Argentina, more and more Russians are choosing to travel to Brazil to give birth to children, who will obtain Brazilian nationality.

item.title: [EU Observer] Europe is trying to ‘replicate’ Silicon Valley. Is it China that offers the better lesson?
item.description: The EU wants Europe's future in European hands, but its flagship scale-up fund leaves the investment strategy to private equity, while China's more targeted venture capital system may offer some better lessons.

item.title: [Financial Times] Has AI broken the old VC model?
item.description: A spate of mega-IPOs triggered by the AI boom is stretching the feast-or-famine industry dynamic to an extreme

item.title: [DW] A war-fatigued and anxious Russia picks a new parliament
item.description: Fuel shortages, drone strikes and mobilization rumors are fueling anxiety and war fatigue in Russia. As support for peace talks grows among Russians, the Kremlin is watching closely ahead of parliamentary elections.

item.title: [EU Observer] Civil partnership from abroad not enough to stay in EU country, according to ECJ preliminary opinion
item.description: As Romania does not recognise same-sex partnerships, having a partner there is not a basis for residency, according to a European Court of Justice opinion on Thursday.

item.title: [EU Observer] Israel triples size of key West Bank settlement, testing von der Leyen’s ‘unacceptable’ rebuke
item.description: The revelation of the West Bank expansion plan came the same day European Commission president Ursula von der Leyen condemned the original, smaller scheme in her State of the Union speech in Strasbourg.

item.title: [EU Observer] EU plans Europe‑wide social media age limits, but can Brussels really police Big Tech?
item.description: A revolution in tech, or another Brussels-bred measure that will fall flat on enforcement? Such has been the debate surrounding the EU's new social media ban for teens, though it is still pending review by law-making bodies.

item.title: [EU Observer] Details emerge on Canada’s ‘associate membership’ EU offer, as Brexit UK left looking on
item.description: EUobserver understands that Ursula von der Leyen did not consult EU governments before making the offer to Canada and there is anxiety in some EU capitals that cosying up to Mark Carney could inflame Donald Trump into re-starting his tariff war with Europe.

item.title: [EU Observer] Russians trying to capture Dobropillia, before the leaves fall from the trees (Ukraine Battlefield update, Day 1,666)
item.description: By concentrating three combined-arms armies and key drone units near Dobropillia, Moscow is gambling on a southern encirclement route that could threaten the Kramatorsk–Sloviansk stronghold without launching a frontal assault.

item.title: [DW] Serbian President Vucic criticizes Kosovo war crimes verdict
item.description: The conviction of four former Kosovo Liberation Army leaders has drawn sharply different reactions across the Balkans. Serbia has accused the court of failing to fully address crimes against Serbs.

item.title: [EU Observer] Orbán re-emerges after long summer holiday, as Magyar strips homophobia from child protection laws (Day 128 of the Tisza government)
item.description: Prime minister Péter Magyar tackles the child protection law, moving to strip the Orban-era conflation of homosexuality with paedophilia from Hungary’s laws.

item.title: [DW] King Charles, Earl Spencer clash over Diana death once again
item.description: Buckingham Palace has rejected criticism of King Charles III in a new book by the brother of his late wife, Princess Diana. Earl Charles Spencer has been a fierce critic of his former brother-in-law for decades.

item.title: [EU Observer] ‘Computer says no’: how Brussels is letting algorithmic social-scoring in by the backdoor
item.description: Just as European courts and regulators are beginning to expose the consequences of a system of algorithmic social scoring, Brussels, with its Digital Omnibus, is considering weakening key safeguards against such automated decision-making on citizens.

item.title: [EU Observer] German chancellor hopes for election gains this Sunday — but CDU may lose votes and Merz his job
item.description: With far-right and far-left forces poised to take votes from the Christian Democrats, pressure is building on German chancellor Friedrich Merz. Sunday's state elections in Berlin and Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania could make or break the leader's prospects of political survival.

item.title: [EU Observer] Listen: After Daphne Caruana Galizia’s murder, why hasn’t justice been done?
item.description: As Daphne Caruana Galizia’s family watches her alleged mastermind walk free for now, Malta’s leaders face mounting fury over whether powerful suspects can ever be convicted for killing a journalist.

item.title: [ECFR] Booted, then suited: Veterans and the making of Putin’s new proto-elite
item.description: The Kremlin is promoting Ukraine war veterans--cultivating a proto-elite who could reinforce Russia’s militarised course.

item.title: [DW] EU seeks Arctic strategy amid growing power rivalry
item.description: Russia's aggression, Trump's threats against Greenland and the race for critical raw materials are pushing the Arctic to the top of Europe's agenda.

item.title: [EU Observer] Sweden begins shipping off prisoners to rented Estonian cells
item.description: While Estonia has prison cells to spare, Sweden's prisons are full. Stockholm will pay €30.6m annually for the first 300 prisoners it sends to a Tartu prison. The deal has been criticised by both countries.

item.title: [EU Observer] Listen: How does the EU plan to ban social media for under-15s?
item.description: The EU Kids Act promises to wean children off endless scrolling and late‑night gaming, but privacy advocates and parts of the tech industry warn the EU’s own age‑verification system could open the door to new risks.

item.title: [ECFR] Ukraine’s Winter of Pressure
item.description: Mark Leonard welcomes Jana Kobzova to discuss the mountain pressure on Ukraine and how Europe can help it weather another wartime winter

item.title: [Financial Times] Venezuela nears deal to move $4bn gold reserve from London to New York
item.description: Agreement would allow interim government of Delcy Rodríguez to access funding

item.title: [Financial Times] Democrats vow to pursue ‘Trump crime family’ after midterm elections
item.description: Lawmaker on oversight committee says he will probe Donald Trump’s sons and Elon Musk if his party takes control of the House

item.title: [Financial Times] Liechtenstein royals threaten lawsuit over dynasty reforms
item.description: Feud in Europe’s wealthiest monarchy deepens after Prince Alois tightens control over family members

item.title: [Financial Times] Medical AI has a proof problem
item.description: The technology’s advances have not yet translated into big improvements in real-life care

item.title: [Politico Europe] EU warns Turkey to clean up waste treatment or face trade ban
item.description: "Serious pollution problems" could lead to suspension of plastic trade with EU's top waste importer.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Deutschlands Kampfjet-Dilemma
item.description: Ein teures Symbol der Abhängigkeit: In Texas nimmt Verteidigungsminister Boris Pistorius den ersten F-35-Kampfjet für die Bundeswehr entgegen. Die Tarnkappenflieger sichern die nukleare Teilhabe Deutschlands, offenbaren aber zugleich das Scheitern europäischer Rüstungsprojekte. Rixa Fürsen erklärt, warum Europa diese technologische Lücke derzeit nicht aus eigener Kraft schließen kann. Nach dem tödlichen Angriff auf einen Zugbegleiter im […]

item.title: [Financial Times] OpenAI breached by researchers using Anthropic models
item.description: Security company hacked into AI lab using tools from its rival

item.title: [Financial Times] Bank of Japan raises rates to 31-year high after Fed move
item.description: Central bank cites inflation risks as it lifts interest rates by 0.25 percentage points to 1.25%

item.title: [Financial Times] OpenAI’s listing delay raises stakes for SoftBank’s $50bn data centre IPO
item.description: Initial public offering of SB Energy set to test investor appetite for Masayoshi Son’s AI gamble

item.title: [Politico Europe] Week Ender: Can Europe patch up the world in disorder?
item.description: The old global order is breaking down. Ursula von der Leyen thinks Europe may have to start building something new around it. In her State of the European Union speech, she floated closer ties with Canada — even “associate membership” — and a new European Security Council, as Europe looks for new ways to work […]

item.title: [Politico Europe] Germany and Spain go head-to-head in EU budget fight
item.description: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz and four other leaders compete with Spanish finance minister in POLITICO articles signaling EU budget deal is still far off.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Germany’s Merz girds for a post-election fight for political survival
item.description: One conservative official predicts "all hell breaks loose" if the ruling CDU fails to win any seats in the regional election in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Five EU leaders: Europe must spend better, not just more
item.description: Bloc’s next budget should cut hundreds of billions from Commission proposal and refocus spending on security, defense and competitiveness.

item.title: [Politico Europe] A common budget that makes common sense
item.description: With Spain for the first time set to become a net contributor to the next EU budget, we are more than willing to pay our fair share to make it a global powerhouse, writes Madrid's finance minister.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Centrist dads Carney and Burnham get ready to take on Trump
item.description: The Canadian leader is now the most popular person in Europe.

item.title: [Politico Europe] What Andy Burnham needs from Donald Trump at their New York meet
item.description: Britain’s new prime minister is set for his first meeting with the U.S. president next Tuesday. Unlike Keir Starmer, he won’t be angling for a second helping.

item.title: [ECFR] Remembering Emma Bonino
item.description: ECFR founding member and co-chair emerita Emma Bonino has died at the age of 78. A towering figure in European foreign policy, she was an inspiration to millions across the continent. She left a deep mark on European and Italian politics, and on ECFR

item.title: [ECFR] The EU’s unfinished business in the Western Balkans
item.description: Montenegro and Albania are moving closer to EU membership. But Brussels should not forget its responsibility towards the Western Balkans as a whole

item.title: [ECFR] The geopolitics of global hunger
item.description: Mark Leonard welcomes Cary Fowler and Jim O’Brien to discuss the factors behind the escalating risk of a major food crisis—and Europe’s role in preventing catastrophe

item.title: [ECFR] Ukraine: The battle beyond war
item.description: Jessica Hendrick welcomes Roman Petrov and Svitlana Zalishchuk to discuss Ukraine’s simultaneous fight for survival on the frontlines and battle for democracy at home
